lessons.title: Scheduling Jobs and Managing a Cleaning Calendar
lessons.body:
A cleaning business lives or dies by its calendar. Without a schedule, you will double-book, miss jobs, and lose clients. Start with a simple paper diary or a free Google Calendar on your phone. For each job, record: client name, address, phone number, date, start time, estimated duration, and price. Also note if the client is weekly, bi-weekly, or once-off. In Africa, many cleaners use WhatsApp to confirm bookings. Send a reminder message the day before: "Hello Mrs. Adeyemi, this is a reminder for your cleaning tomorrow at 9am. Please confirm." This reduces no-shows.

Group jobs by area. If you have three clients in Lekki, schedule them on the same day. This saves transport money and time. For example, if you clean a house in Ikoyi from 8am to 11am, then another in Victoria Island from 12pm to 3pm, and a third in Lekki from 4pm to 6pm, you can move between them easily. Avoid criss-crossing the city. Use a map app like Google Maps to check travel time between jobs. Always add a 30-minute buffer for traffic or overruns.

Set realistic durations. A 3-bedroom apartment takes 3-4 hours for a deep clean, but only 2 hours for a maintenance clean. A small office of 5 rooms takes 2 hours. If you underestimate, you will rush and do a poor job. If you overestimate, you lose money. Track your actual times for one month and adjust.

Use colour codes in your calendar: green for confirmed, yellow for pending, red for cancelled. At the end of each week, review the next week's schedule. Call any client who hasn't confirmed. Also, block out time for travel, supply shopping, and rest. You cannot work 7 days a week. Schedule at least one day off.

Finally, keep a waiting list. If a client cancels, you can call someone on the waiting list to fill the slot. This keeps your income stable. A good calendar is your most important tool. It prevents chaos and helps you look professional.

lessons.title: Route Planning to Minimize Travel Time and Costs
lessons.body:
In many African cities, transport is expensive and traffic is unpredictable. A cleaner who plans routes saves money and time. The goal is to clean more houses in less travel time. Start by mapping all your clients on a free app like Google My Maps. Mark each client's location. Then group them by neighbourhood. For example, if you have clients in Surulere, Yaba, and Ebute Metta, those are close together. Schedule them on the same day. Do not go from Ajah to Ikeja in one morningâthat is a waste.

Plan your route in a loop. Start with the farthest client, then work your way back home. Or start with the nearest and end with the farthest. The key is to avoid backtracking. Use a map app to check real-time traffic. In Lagos, traffic peaks from 6-9am and 4-7pm. If possible, schedule jobs outside these times. For example, clean an office from 7-9am before traffic, then a home from 10am-1pm, then another from 2-5pm.

Consider public transport costs. A bus from Oshodi to Ikeja costs about â¦500, while a keke from Ikeja to Ogba costs â¦300. If you have three clients in one area, you pay one transport cost instead of three. That saves you â¦1,000 or more per day. You can also negotiate with a taxi driver for a daily rate if you have many stops.

Keep a travel log. For one week, record how long it takes to travel between each client. You will see patterns. Maybe you always get stuck on a certain road. Adjust your schedule to avoid that road. Also, consider carrying your supplies in a compact bag or trolley. If you use public transport, a trolley is easier than many buckets.

Finally, communicate with clients about your arrival time. If you are running late due to traffic, send a quick WhatsApp message: "I am stuck in traffic, I will arrive at 10:15 instead of 10:00." Clients appreciate honesty. Good route planning means more jobs per day, lower transport costs, and less stress.

lessons.title: Inventory Management for Cleaning Supplies and Equipment
lessons.body:
If you run out of bleach in the middle of a job, you look unprofessional. Inventory management means always having the right supplies, in the right amounts, without wasting money on excess. Start by listing everything you use: bleach, dish soap, floor cleaner, glass cleaner, toilet cleaner, sponges, scrubbing brushes, mops, buckets, gloves, masks, and cloths. For each item, note how much you use per job. For example, one 750ml bottle of bleach lasts about 10 standard jobs. A mop lasts 3 months if used daily.

Buy in bulk when you can. In many African markets, like Balogun in Lagos or Kariakoo in Dar es Salaam, you get a discount if you buy a carton of 12 bottles. But only buy what you can store safely. Bleach and other chemicals should be kept in a cool, dry place, away from children and food. Use a locked cupboard if possible. Label everything clearly. Never transfer chemicals into unmarked bottlesâthat is dangerous.

Create a simple inventory sheet. Use a notebook or a free app like Google Sheets. Every time you use a supply, write it down. At the end of each week, check your stock. If you have less than two weeks' supply, reorder. For equipment, check for wear and tear. A mop with frayed strings does not clean well. Replace it. A vacuum cleaner needs its filter cleaned monthly.

Consider a "supply kit" for each team. If you have employees, give each a plastic crate with a standard set of supplies. They are responsible for keeping it stocked. You can check the kit at the end of the week. This reduces theft and waste.

Keep a small emergency fund for supplies. Prices fluctuate. If you suddenly get three new clients, you may need extra bleach and cloths. Having â¦5,000 set aside for supplies prevents last-minute panic. Also, buy reusable cloths instead of paper towels. They save money and are better for the environment. A pack of 10 microfibre cloths costs about â¦2,000 and lasts months.

Finally, track your supply costs as a percentage of your income. If you earn â¦50,000 in a month and spend â¦10,000 on supplies, that is 20%. Try to keep it under 15%. If it is higher, look for cheaper suppliers or reduce waste.

lessons.title: Setting Up a Client Communication System
lessons.body:
Clients want to know you are reliable. A simple communication system keeps them happy and reduces misunderstandings. The easiest tool is WhatsApp. It is free, widely used, and allows voice notes, photos, and location sharing. Create a business WhatsApp account with a professional profile photo and a clear status: "Home & Office Cleaning â Available Mon-Sat." Use a separate phone number for business if possible.

For each client, save their name and address in your contacts. When you confirm a booking, send a standard message: "Hello [Name], your cleaning is confirmed for [date] at [time]. Our team will arrive with all supplies. Please let us know if you have any special requests." After the job, send a follow-up: "Thank you for choosing us. How was the cleaning? We appreciate your feedback." This shows you care.

Use a simple client log. In a notebook or Google Sheet, record: client name, phone, address, frequency, price, and any notes (e.g., "allergic to bleach," "has a dog," "prefers morning slots"). Before each visit, check the notes. This personal touch makes clients loyal.

For reminders, set a recurring alarm on your phone. One day before the job, send a reminder. If the client does not respond within 2 hours, call them. Do not assume they remember. In Africa, many people have multiple commitments. A gentle reminder prevents no-shows.

If you have employees, create a group chat for the team. Post the daily schedule each morning. Use voice notes for instructions if typing is hard. But keep client information privateâdo not share phone numbers in the group.

Handle complaints quickly. If a client says something was missed, apologize and offer to fix it within 24 hours. Do not argue. A bad review spreads fast. A good recovery can turn a complaint into a loyal client.

Finally, ask for testimonials. After a few good jobs, send: "If you are happy with our service, would you mind writing a short review? It helps us grow." You can then share these reviews on your WhatsApp status or Facebook page. Good communication builds trust and brings referrals.

lessons.title: Handling Cancellations, Rescheduling, and No-Shows
lessons.body:
Cancellations and no-shows cost you money. If a client cancels at the last minute, you lose that slot and the transport you may have already paid. You need a clear policy. When you book a client, tell them: "Please give at least 24 hours' notice if you need to cancel or reschedule. Late cancellations may incur a 50% fee." This is common in many businesses. It encourages clients to respect your time.

If a client cancels with enough notice, offer to reschedule immediately. Say: "No problem. Would you like to move to Thursday at the same time?" This keeps the job. If they cancel without notice, send a polite message: "We missed you today. As per our policy, a 50% fee applies. Would you like to reschedule?" Some clients will pay. Others may argue. Stay calm and professional. If they refuse, you may choose to waive the fee for a first-time offence, but note it.

For no-shows, where you arrive and the client is not home, wait 15 minutes. Call and send a WhatsApp message. If no response, leave. Send a message: "We arrived at 9am but could not reach you. Please contact us to reschedule. A no-show fee may apply." Do not waste more than 30 minutes.

Track cancellations. If a client cancels three times in a row, they are not serious. You can politely stop offering them prime slots. Focus on reliable clients. Also, keep a waiting list. If someone cancels, call a waiting-list client to fill the slot. You can offer a small discount for same-day booking.

If you have employees, pay them for the travel time if a client cancels late. This keeps morale up. You can add a clause in your client agreement that late cancellations cover labour costs.

Finally, be flexible but firm. Sometimes emergencies happen. If a regular client has a genuine emergency, waive the fee once. But do not let clients take advantage. A clear policy, communicated upfront, prevents most problems.

lessons.title: Developing Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for Cleaning Tasks
lessons.body:
An SOP is a step-by-step guide for how to do a task. It ensures every cleaner does the same quality work, even if you are not there. Start with the most common tasks: cleaning a bathroom, cleaning a kitchen, dusting, mopping, and vacuuming. For each, write the steps in order. Use simple language. For example, a bathroom SOP might be: 1. Put on gloves. 2. Spray toilet cleaner inside bowl and let sit. 3. Spray all-purpose cleaner on sink, counter, and outside of toilet. 4. Scrub toilet bowl with brush, flush. 5. Wipe sink and counter with cloth. 6. Wipe toilet exterior. 7. Spray shower and tub, scrub, rinse. 8. Mop floor with disinfectant. 9. Remove gloves, wash hands.

Include safety notes. For example, "Never mix bleach and ammoniaâit creates toxic gas." "Use a mask when dusting." "Lift with your knees, not your back." These protect your team.

Write SOPs for equipment use too. How to use a vacuum cleaner: check bag, plug in, move slowly, empty after use. How to use a mop: dip in bucket, wring well, mop in sections, change water when dirty. This prevents damage and saves supplies.

Test your SOPs. Have a new cleaner follow them while you watch. If they miss a step, the SOP is not clear. Revise it. Keep SOPs in a plastic sleeve or a WhatsApp group so everyone can access them. You can also make short videos on your phone showing each step. That is even better for visual learners.

Review SOPs every 3 months. If you find a faster or better way, update them. For example, you might switch from a string mop to a flat mop, which is quicker. Update the SOP accordingly.

SOPs also help you train new staff quickly. Instead of explaining everything, you just give them the SOP. They can read it and practice. This saves you time and ensures consistency. Clients notice when the same quality is delivered every time. That is how you build a reputation.

quiz.q: What is the best way to reduce no-shows?
options: A) Call the client every hour before the job
B) Send a reminder message the day before
quiz.explanation: A reminder the day before gives the client time to confirm or reschedule, reducing last-minute surprises.

quiz.q: Why should you group jobs by area?
options: A) To charge more per job
B) To save transport money and time
quiz.explanation: Grouping jobs in the same area reduces travel distance and cost, allowing more jobs per day.

quiz.q: How long does a deep clean of a 3-bedroom apartment typically take?
quiz.explanation: A deep clean requires more time for detailed work, usually 3-4 hours for a 3-bedroom apartment.

quiz.q: What colour code is suggested for a confirmed job in your calendar?
quiz.explanation: Green indicates a confirmed booking, making it easy to see your secured jobs.

quiz.q: What should you do if a client cancels with less than 24 hours' notice?
options: A) Ignore it and never book them again
B) Charge a 50% fee as per your policy
C) Clean their house for free next time
D) Report them to the police
quiz.explanation: A clear late-cancellation fee discourages last-minute cancellations and compensates you for lost time.

quiz.q: What is the main benefit of route planning?
options: A) You can visit more clients in less time
B) You can charge higher prices
C) You never get stuck in traffic
D) You can work 7 days a week
quiz.explanation: Efficient routes reduce travel time, allowing you to fit more jobs into a day.

quiz.q: When is traffic typically heaviest in Lagos?
quiz.explanation: Rush hour in Lagos is generally 6-9am and 4-7pm, so schedule jobs outside these times if possible.

quiz.q: How can you save on transport costs when visiting multiple clients?
options: B) Use a taxi for each trip
C) Schedule clients in the same area on the same day
D) Only take jobs within walking distance
quiz.explanation: Grouping clients in one area means you pay one transport cost instead of multiple trips.

quiz.q: What should you do if you are running late due to traffic?
options: A) Say nothing and arrive late
B) Send a quick WhatsApp message to the client
D) Blame the client for living far
quiz.explanation: Informing the client shows respect and helps manage their expectations.

quiz.q: Why is a trolley useful for a cleaner using public transport?
options: C) It is cheaper than a bag
D) It can be used as a seat
quiz.explanation: A trolley makes it easier to transport multiple cleaning supplies on public transport.

quiz.q: How often should you check your inventory?
quiz.explanation: A weekly check helps you reorder before running out, avoiding mid-job shortages.

quiz.q: Where should you store cleaning chemicals?
options: A) In the kitchen near food
B) In a cool, dry, locked cupboard
quiz.explanation: A cool, dry, locked cupboard keeps chemicals safe from children and prevents degradation.

quiz.q: What is a good target for supply costs as a percentage of income?
quiz.explanation: Keeping supply costs under 15% of income helps maintain profitability.

quiz.q: Why are reusable microfibre cloths better than paper towels?
options: A) They are cheaper in the long run
D) They are required by law
quiz.explanation: Microfibre cloths can be washed and reused many times, saving money over disposable paper towels.

quiz.q: What is the best tool for client communication in many African countries?
quiz.explanation: WhatsApp is widely used, free, and allows quick messages, voice notes, and photos.

quiz.q: What should you do after completing a job?
options: A) Send a follow-up message asking for feedback
B) Immediately ask for a tip
D) Post a photo on social media without permission
quiz.explanation: A follow-up shows you care and gives the client a chance to provide feedback or request a fix.

quiz.q: Why should you keep a client log?
options: A) To remember personal details and preferences
B) To sell to other companies
C) To report to the government
quiz.explanation: A client log helps you personalise service and avoid mistakes like using a banned product.

quiz.q: What should you do if a client complains about a missed spot?
options: C) Apologise and offer to fix it within 24 hours
quiz.explanation: A quick, sincere recovery can turn a complaint into loyalty and positive word-of-mouth.

quiz.q: What is a good way to get testimonials?
options: A) Demand them after every job
B) Ask happy clients for a short review
D) Only ask on social media
quiz.explanation: Asking satisfied clients for a review is honest and provides social proof.

quiz.q: What should you do if a client cancels with enough notice?
quiz.explanation: Offering to reschedule keeps the client and fills your calendar.

quiz.q: How long should you wait if a client is not home for a scheduled cleaning?
quiz.explanation: Waiting 15 minutes is reasonable; after that, call and message, then leave if no response.

quiz.q: What is a no-show fee?
options: A) A fee charged when a client is not home
B) A fee for using the toilet
D) A fee for extra supplies
quiz.explanation: A no-show fee compensates you for travel and lost time when a client is absent.

quiz.q: What should you do if a client cancels three times in a row?
options: A) Stop offering them prime slots
C) Clean their house for free
D) Report them to the police
quiz.explanation: Frequent cancellations mean the client is not serious; focus on reliable clients instead.

quiz.q: What is an SOP?
options: A) A step-by-step guide for a task
B) A type of cleaning chemical
quiz.explanation: SOP stands for Standard Operating Procedure, a written guide to ensure consistent quality.

quiz.q: Why should you never mix bleach and ammonia?
quiz.explanation: Mixing bleach and ammonia produces chloramine gas, which is dangerous to breathe.

quiz.q: How often should you review and update your SOPs?
quiz.explanation: Regular review ensures SOPs reflect best practices and any new equipment or methods.

quiz.q: What is the first step in a bathroom cleaning SOP?
quiz.explanation: Putting on gloves first protects your hands from chemicals and germs.

quiz.q: Why are SOPs useful for training new staff?
options: A) They save time and ensure consistency
B) They replace the need for payment
C) They are required by law
D) They make the job harder
quiz.explanation: New staff can read and follow SOPs, reducing the need for one-on-one training and ensuring quality.

quiz.q: What should you include in a kitchen cleaning SOP?
options: A) Steps for cleaning counters, sink, stove, and floor
B) How to cook a meal
C) How to fix a refrigerator
D) How to paint the walls
quiz.explanation: A kitchen SOP covers cleaning surfaces, appliances, and floors in a logical order.

quiz.q: What is a good way to make SOPs easy to access for your team?
options: A) Keep them in a locked safe
B) Share them in a WhatsApp group or plastic sleeve
D) Write them on a napkin
quiz.explanation: Digital or laminated copies ensure everyone can access and refer to SOPs easily.
